articles.title: My dad was a monster! Sara Karloff on reviving Frankenstein, 95 years on
articles.summary: Boris Karloff’s daughter and composer Michael Shapiro, whose musical score for the 1931 film is finally coming to London, talk about how it became a much-loved classic.
body: Once seen, never forgotten – the 1931 Frankenstein is 95 years old, but still one of the most instantly recognisable of classic horrors. Whether it’s the sight of lanky Boris Karloff lumbering into the frame with his squared-off head, neck bolts and oversized leaden shoes, or the sound of a thunderclap and Colin Clive exclaiming “It’s alive!” as the monster comes to life one stormy night in the laboratory – the film still raises hairs on the back of the neck.

However, this classic has arguably long been missing one element: a continuous musical soundtrack – the original movie had dialogue but no music. In 2001, the American composer Michael Shapiro wrote a full-length score, which he will be conducting alongside the film for the first time in London next month, at Cadogan Hall with the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. “It becomes one artistic expression, one artistic experience,” he says. “The film and the music, together, and the audience forgets that I am there.” Shapiro says his music emphasises what is already up on the screen. “Suddenly the film jumps out in a way it never did before.”
points: Boris Karloff’s daughter and composer Michael Shapiro, whose musical score for the 1931 film is finally coming to London, talk about how it became a much-loved classic.

articles.title: ‘She never accepted no’: Liam Neeson on dogged heroine behind Tuam mass baby grave film
articles.summary: Catherine Corless’s exposure of almost 800 infant deaths at a home led by nuns prompted Neeson to bring the story to screen. Liam Neeson still remembers his shock and shame when he read a New York Times article about the mother and baby institution in Tuam, County Galway.
body: It was 2017 and the article chronicled the campaign by Catherine Corless, an amateur local historian, to expose abuse and neglect by Irish nuns that led to hundreds of children being buried in a mass, unmarked grave.

“I had such a visceral reaction,” Neeson told the Guardian. “I’m obviously Irish, I was raised in the Catholic church, and I had a deep sense of embarrassment and obligation for the truth to come out and for there to be some accountability.”

It prompted the actor – and former altar boy – to use his heft in the film industry to become a producer for the first time. He optioned the article, visited Corless at her home and assembled a team to put the story on screen.

The result, nine years later, is The Lost Children of Tuam, a feature film that is released in Ireland this week and in the UK next month. “This was such an important story for the world to know about and to give a voice to the hundreds of babies and children that died,” said Neeson.

articles.title: ‘Florid’ Director Billy Lumby on Challenging ‘Misrepresentation’ of Schizophrenia on Screen and Casting Non-Actors in Feature Debut
articles.summary: The depiction of schizophrenia on screen — especially in horror movies — has largely seen the mental health condition linked to violent and unpredictable rages, showing people when something has gone horribly wrong.
body: While the story doesn’t culminate in the violent depths seen in the cinema tropes Lumby was purposefully looking to avoid, it’s a tough watch. But that’s largely due to the aural sensation provided by the voices, which become more powerful and prominent as the film progresses, dragging Jamal down with them.

Carrying “Florid” as Jamal is Jonathan Jules, best known for Steve McQueen’s “Small Axe,” in his first lead role. “It’s not easy to act in a mentally unwell state in an authentic, accurate way,” notes Lumby.

During filming, Jules wore earpieces on set, with actors in another room speaking into microphones so he could hear the voices live and respond in an unrestricted way. “There were theses little moments where his eyes twitched — it just made if feel so real,” says Lumby. After principal photography wrapped, many months would be spent in post-production augmenting the voices to create the right tone and weave them into the overall soundscape.

articles.summary: Former BBC journalist Naima Mohamud’s heartfelt and warm comedy “Halima,” about a 10-year-old Somali girl trying to fit in Finland in 1998 took home Helsinki’s Finnish Film Affair’s top prize for Best Fiction on Thursday evening. The award was handed out by the jury, including U.S.

“This is the same here, and we simply had to make this movie,” added Pösö, who produces with Finland’s No-Office Films, in co-production with Ireland’s Vico Films.

“This story was inspired by my family, and my experience of growing up in Finland, where no one had seen black people!” said Dublin and Helsinki-based Mohamud, who studied filmmaking at London Metropolitan University and USC (University of Southern California) in Los Angeles. The feature, which won Best Pitch at the Haugesund New Nordic Films in 2024, is now in post-production with a delivery set for the fall 2027.

At Thursday’s awards ceremony, which closed the showcase day at Helsinki Film Festival’s industry confab Finnish Film Affair, the jury also handed out the €3,000 ($3,400) Best Nordic Film Award from the Amos Anderson Fund to the Norwegian suspense drama “11 Hours” by Emilie Beck, best-known for Netflix’s “Royalteen” and TV2 Norway’s hit “ Escaping Bolivia.”

articles.title: ‘Unabomber’ Review: A Portrait of the Terrorist as a Young Man, Given a Hokey TV-Movie Gloss
articles.summary: The Unabomber may be a figure of enduring public fascination, but it’s hard to see that extending to “Unabomber,” Netflix’s unimaginatively titled and prosaically assembled drama about how domestic terrorist Ted Kaczynski was radicalized, and how he was caught.
body: Jacob Tremblay doesn't convince as the teenage Ted Kaczynski in this Netflix filler, which alternates a semi-interesting psychological origin story with a by-the-numbers procedural following his capture.

There’s certainly little in the film to match the intensity of Tony Stone’s underseen 2021 biopic “Ted K,” starring a genuinely disquieting Sharlto Copley in the title role, which worked precisely because it didn’t try to crack or psychologize Kaczynski in the ways that “Unabomber” does to increasingly banal effect. While Miller pores over Kaczynski’s famous manifesto, correctly concluding that its linguistic quirks will lead the authorities to him, the upshot of Murray’s study four decades before is that the young Kaczynski shows signs of schizophrenia. Neither qualifies as a eureka moment likely to make slumping viewers sit bolt upright on their couch.

body: The Greek adaptation of the series is produced by Primavisione and stars Maria Nafpliotou (“Café 404”), Charis Fragulis (“Afterlov”), Nikos Psarras (“The Fire Bracelet”), and Paschalis Terzis. In addition to “The Others,” Greece will also get a local adaptation of the telenovela “All The Flowers,” with the same production company and broadcasting channel.

To follow the start of production, author Lucas Paraizo visited the set in Greece: “I was on the set of the Greek version of ‘The Others’, a series I created, and had the pleasure of watching the shooting of one of the most important scenes of the first season: the scene where the characters Cibele and Wando face off over their sons’ fight,” he said.

“I had the pleasure of witnessing the enthusiasm of the cast, crew, and director Alexandro Avranas, whom I’ve been a fan of since he directed the feature film ‘Miss Violence,’” he added. “I am curious to see this new version of the series and am sure it will be a success in Greece, as it was in Brazil, countries that have a lot in common.”

articles.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer
articles.summary: Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators. Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic…
body: Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of Aardman Animations seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets from Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.
Sought-after items included Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models from the Bristol studio’s hugely popular 2024 film Vengeance Most Fowl.

Lot 216, for example, was Wallace in his traditional outfit of a knitted green tank top, red tie and brown trousers. The catalogue said he was in “smashing condition”, and gave details of his construction: “Wallace’s head is moulded from clay; while his body is made of silicone to facilitate smooth repositioning by the animators.

“He has a skeleton, just like every salt-of-the-earth lad, it’s just that his happens to be made of metal. His teeth, shirt collar, tie, pen, and pencil are fast-cast resin and his eyes are plastic.” It sold for an eye-popping £50,400.
points: Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators.

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones bases new role on funny Welsh people she knows
articles.summary: Zeta-Jones plays Jackie Price, a former cocaine dealer who is targeted by assassins, in Kill Jackie.
body: Actor Catherine Zeta-Jones says she based her performance in the new series Kill Jackie on people she knows in Wales.
The Mumbles star plays Jackie Price, a former cocaine dealer who is being targeted by hitmen, in a new series for Prime.
It is the first time she has played a role using her Swansea accent, external and the first time she has filmed a drama in Wales.
"I played on people I know in Wales, people who are comedic and the accent makes it funny and real and true, but the character comes from a tough side of Swansea, which we do have as well," she said.

articles.title: British rapper Yung Filly to face rape retrial in Australia next June
articles.summary: Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos was cleared of several sexual offences in July but a jury was undecided on three rape charges.
body: British rapper Yung Filly will face a rape retrial in Australia next June after a jury failed to reach a verdict during an earlier trial.

In July, a jury acquitted the 31-year-old - whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos - of three counts of rape, one of assault and one of strangulation but found him guilty of two assault charges. No decision was reached for three rape charges, which he has denied.
A fan, aged 20 at the time, alleges Barrientos repeatedly raped and assaulted her in his hotel room in Perth, Western Australia, after a 2024 concert.
The court previously heard that Barrientos and the woman had consensual sex before she alleged it turned violent and he refused to stop.

articles.title: ‘I get lost going to the bathroom’: John Hannah on world travel, stealing props and being ‘the Scottish Eminem’
articles.summary: The Four Weddings and a Funeral actor answers your questions on being confused with James Nesbitt, his own Sliding Doors moment and a new perspective since turning 60. How often do you get asked to recite that WH Auden poem from Four Weddings and a Funeral, and can you do it from memory right now?
body: In Steve Coogan ’s Paul Calf’s Video Diary, your character praises Orson Welles’ The Trial for its “tremendous energy”, while Paul says he would “rather watch Dave Lee Travis playing Macbeth”. What’s your actual opinion of The Trial [by Franz Kafka]? AdrianH1 God, it’s a long time since I’ve read that. I read a lot of those books in my younger days, but probably, like a lot of people, even those who are graduates of English literature, I’d be hard pushed these days to tell you what it was about, other than the persecution of some minor character.

As a popular jobbing actor, you have a massive list of credits. Has anyone ever come up to you to express their appreciation for a certain role and you had no idea what they were on about? Kevcoe No. It’s always heartwarming when somebody comes up and offers their congratulations on something a little bit lower down the pecking order. Fortunately, people rarely ever come up to tell me that they thought I was shit in something. I quite often get Paul Calf’s Video Diary, and that Macbeth line. To be frank, I can’t quite remember the context.

articles.title: Media outlets banned by Trump denied access to White House dinner despite judge's order
articles.summary: CNN and MS NOW reporters say they were barred from covering a state dinner after a judge ruled their passes should be restored.
body: CNN and MS NOW reporters say they have been denied entry to cover a White House state dinner despite a judge ruling their access to the grounds must be restored.

A federal judge said in an overnight ruling that the White House ban on three outlets - CNN and MS NOW and Politico - was likely unconstitutional and that the administration must allow them access, for now. Trump barred them last week, accusing them of "fake news".
Journalists with the three outlets were allowed back in on Thursday morning.
Then in the evening, a CNN reporter and a producer and an MS NOW reporter said that they were denied entry to cover the guests arriving for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
